assessment.report:
# Role invocation: scoped development readiness

The user approved active-session availability checks, explicit named-role selection without silent generic fallback, invocation reconciliation and mandatory final actual child-agent output. Existing architecture and shared contracts were sufficient for this bounded correction. No structural refactor, new orchestration runtime, PRD, OpenSpec adoption or model/configuration change was required. Lead owned shared Skill/validator edits; the named Tester owned isolated regression tests and the stage packet; the named Reviewer performed independent semantic review.

Reviewed the changed shared role/execution/template/handoff contracts, six Team entrypoints, README operating rules, release policy and package validator/test changes. All expected routing targets are preserved. Source package validation passed. The Tester observed an actual initial Red when a valid replacement link concealed a lost Team role route, then Green across six omitted routes and restoration. Missing handoff coverage preserves an existing guard rather than claiming a new Red. Isolated stage-verification, documentation and fake-home installation regressions passed and fixtures were removed. Code-comment self-check covered the validator file overview and new routing block explanation; no new public interface was added. Tester scenario/expected-result comments match new assertions.

The Reviewer checked five hypothetical applications, not five extra agent invocations. An immediate wrong-selector pause was strengthened after review; no remaining material finding was reported. Actual current-task children were /root/role_checks, explicitly selected as team-tester, and /root/role_review, explicitly selected as team-reviewer; both completed. Created failures, retries and generic replacements did not occur. The stage packet records their tasks, known statuses and honest unknown metadata.

Active Tester/Reviewer tool definitions advertise GPT-6 Sol profiles, while source TOMLs expect GPT-6.1 Sol at the same efforts. Resolved runtime identity/model was not returned. This discrepancy is disclosed environment evidence, not a claim of loaded source profiles or an authorized model change. Exact model-allocation verification and future runtime scenarios remain unverified/manual pending. No actual installation, commit or push was performed.

This is a current task-scoped documentation readiness assessment, not whole-project certification or manual acceptance. Other capability documents remain in place without re-certification or obsolete/legacy decisions. No substantive requirement ambiguity blocks this completed scope. Existing earlier scoped reviews must still pass their own freshness checks before reuse. Authored records and static checks detect changes and preserve discovery routes; they cannot authenticate user approval, actual loaded identity or enforce an unbypassable runtime gate. A minimal redacted local feedback record was saved, without source contents or public home paths.
